The inverse problem is modeled as a nonlinear ill-conditioned system F(x) = y with additive noise y_obs = F(x) + noise.
The forward electromagnetic scattering problem is governed by the time-harmonic Maxwell equations with refractive index n(r) = 1 - a(r).
The unknown perturbation a(r) is supported in the unit ball and assumed C1,α-smooth, real, and positive.
The data vector y has dimension N = 5000, derived from 25 incident waves and 100 measurement directions.
Regularized Newton methods considered include Levenberg-Marquardt (b=0) and IRGNM (b = x0 - x).
The regularization parameter γ_k is chosen as γ_0 * γ^{-k} with γ > 1.
The CG method is used for solving linearized systems, exploiting its connection to Lanczos' method for eigenvalue approximations.
Spectral preconditioners are constructed using a subset J of Ritz pairs approximating large isolated eigenvalues of GᵀG.
The spectrum of the preconditioned matrix clusters at 1 with multiplicity equal to the number of eigenpairs used in the preconditioner.
Lanczos' method approximates eigenvalues well for isolated eigenvalues but less so for clustered ones.
Preconditioner updates are necessary due to multiple isolated eigenvalues and decreasing regularization parameter.
The Lepski˘ı-type stopping rule uses estimates of propagated noise error based on the covariance matrix of noise.
The discrepancy principle stops iterations when the residual norm falls below τ times the noise level δ, but can fail for large data dimensions.
Numerical experiments show the Lepski˘ı stopping rule outperforms the discrepancy principle for noisy data.
The forward problem is solved using a fast solver for the electromagnetic Lippmann-Schwinger equation with up to 786,432 degrees of freedom.
The unknown refractive index perturbation is parameterized by 500 to 2000 coefficients using splines and spherical harmonics.
The Jacobian matrix is not computed explicitly; only matrix-vector multiplications with A and Aᵀ are used.
The preconditioner M is defined as M = γ I + Σ_{j∈J} λ_j u_j u_jᵀ, where λ_j and u_j are eigenpairs of AᵀA.
The CG method with preconditioning uses a stopping criterion ensuring relative accuracy ε/(1-ε).
Reorthogonalization via Householder transformations is used to maintain numerical stability in CG and Lanczos computations.
Initial Newton steps may use Newton-CG without freezing the Jacobian for better globalization.
The spectral preconditioner is applied symmetrically as M^{-1/2} Gᵀ G M^{-1/2} for stability during updates.
The Ritz values used for updates are selected if they are well separated from the cluster at 1, typically ≥ 1.1.
The paper provides an algorithmic framework combining spectral preconditioning, iterative regularization, and Lepski˘ı stopping.
